risks: CRITICAL: Expo + pnpm symlink handling — Expo SDK 52+ supports monorepos automatically, but if transitive dependencies fail to resolve in the isolated pnpm store, builds will fail silently until nodeLinker: hoisted is set. This is a gotcha: the fix is easy but the debugging is slow. Recommend: test with isolated first, fall back to hoisted if module-not-found errors appear.

MODERATE: API client type divergence — web app has hand-written response types in api.ts; mobile will need identical types. If the API evolves, both must be updated. No single source of truth. Consider: could @huntstack/shared export API response types generated from the Fastify schema?

MODERATE: CORS origin for local development — API defaults to localhost:3000; mobile dev server and emulator will have different origins. Without VITE_API_URL, mobile must use hardcoded config. Consider: environment-based URL selection at build/runtime.

LOW: CI will not auto-pick up apps/mobile — CI names packages explicitly. New package will be invisible to typecheck/build/test jobs until ci.yml is edited. Not a blocker, but requires human follow-up.

LOW: Claude hooks only check API tsc — editing mobile TypeScript files will not trigger type-checking. Not a blocker if mobile has its own tsconfig and the builder remembers to run it; consider: should we add a hook matcher for *mobile* files too?
LOW: localStorage usage in web app (ChatPage line 40) — mobile must use AsyncStorage or similar. Plan ahead for abstraction if you want to share conversation history between web and mobile.

POTENTIAL: If the monorepo uses pnpm's public-hoist-pattern or shamefully-hoist for any reason in the future, Metro's symlink support may break. Check before adding either setting to .npmrc or pnpm-workspace.yaml.
scout.verdict: SCOUT COMPLETE. The repo structure is ready for a mobile workspace member. No fundamental blockers found. The Expo + pnpm symlink issue is a known pattern now (2026); modern Expo handles it. The API client is web-specific (Vite env vars) but easy to rewrite for RN. CI will need manual updates. Recommend: start with isolated pnpm, test Metro resolution, fall back to hoisted if needed. API endpoint surface for first release (4 pages x ~8-10 endpoints) is well-defined.

plan.intent: Hand-write a mobile-only API client covering ONLY the v1 endpoints, plus the runtime base-URL mechanism. apps/web/src/lib/api.ts cannot be copied - line 1 is import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL, which does not exist in React Native, and the file is ~700 lines of inline response types for ~40 endpoints we do not need. Write a fresh ~150-line client at apps/mobile/src/lib/api.ts covering exactly five endpoints: GET /api/species, GET /api/geo/zip/:zip, GET /api/geo/search, GET /api/geo/reverse, GET /api/hunt/recommendations. Carry over the two good behaviours from the web client - the AbortController 30s timeout and the response-not-ok error unwrap - and nothing else. TAKE THE workspace:* DEPENDENCY on @huntstack/shared and use it for real: import calculateDistance (packages/shared/src/index.ts:234) instead of re-implementing haversine the way WhereToHuntPage.tsx:9 did, getStateName for state labels, and formatDateRange for season dates. This is legal - apps/mobile and packages/shared are the SAME app (huntstack); the umbrella invariant forbids cross-APP imports, not intra-app workspace deps. It is also deliberate risk retirement: a workspace:* dep on a raw-TS, no-build package is exactly the thing Metro pnpm symlink handling either resolves or does not, and the Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions inside formatDateRange is scout unknown 2 - using both in v1 answers both questions now instead of in run 2. BASE URL MECHANISM (decision, do not re-litigate): process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL, inlined by the Expo bundler - no app.config.ts plumbing, no expo-constants extra block. Dev default when that var is unset: derive the LAN host from expo-constants Constants.expoConfig.hostUri (the Metro dev-server host, e.g. 192.168.x.x:8081), take the hostname, and build http://HOSTNAME:4000. This is what makes a physical phone and an emulator work out of the box - http://localhost:4000 is unreachable from both, and apps/api already binds HOST 0.0.0.0 (scout fact 12) so the LAN address is already served. NEVER hardcode a production URL: CURRENT_STATE.md:299 records that the production domain lives only in Cloudflare/Railway env vars and not in the repo. In a production build with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL unset, throw a clear configuration error rather than falling back to anything. Ship apps/mobile/.env.example documenting the var; never commit .env. Add vitest (node environment, pure logic only - no component rendering) mirroring the precedent apps/api already sets, with tests for the query-string builder, the error unwrap, and the hostUri-to-baseUrl derivation including the unset-in-prod throw.

architect.rationale:
SHAPE: single-loop, parallel_safe false. This is the honest answer and I want to be plain about why, because a diamond was available and I am declining it.

huntstack IS a git repo (main at 6d6a98a, clean), so branch isolation is technically permitted - the blocker is not isolation, it is that there are no files to be disjoint about. Scout fact 6 is decisive: apps/mobile/ does not exist. Slice 1 must create package.json, app.json, tsconfig.json, the expo-router app/ tree and a repo-wide pnpm install. Slices 2, 3 and 4 all live inside files that do not exist until that finishes. Three builders started from main in parallel worktrees would each find a tree with no apps/mobile/ in it, each run create-expo-app themselves, and produce three different scaffolds with three different resolved SDK versions and three mutually conflicting regenerations of pnpm-lock.yaml. The fan-in would be garbage. That is a chain in a diamond costume, and the disjoint-file-set test it fails is not a technicality: I cannot name the disjoint sets because at plan time the union of all of them is the empty set. There is a second, independent reason - the two shared files in this run (pnpm-lock.yaml and ci.yml) would be contended by any fan-out, and pnpm-lock.yaml in particular does not merge. Three parallel installs produce three lockfiles and git will conflict on all of them.

WHY THIS v1 CUT AND NOT A BIGGER ONE. The cut is Killer Feature 1 only - Where should I hunt this weekend - plus the scaffold that had to exist anyway. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) Positioning: huntstack/CLAUDE.md:51 says they own in-field tools, we own pre-hunt intelligence, and :57 lists KF1 as the flagship and LIVE. Of the three killer features, KF1 is the one whose value goes UP on a phone specifically - it is location-aware, it is the query a hunter runs the night before or from a truck, and expo-location gives it a better answer than the browser geolocation prompt the web page uses. (2) API surface: KF1 needs five endpoints (species, three geo, hunt recommendations). MigrationPage needs eleven and is chart-heavy time-series work that is desktop-shaped. ChatPage needs four plus conversation persistence. Five endpoints is a client one builder can hand-write correctly in one sitting; eleven is where the type-divergence risk scout flagged as MODERATE actually bites. (3) I explicitly declined the easy port. HomePage hits zero endpoints and would have been the cheapest possible first screen - it is a static marketing page, and shipping it would prove nothing about whether this architecture works. The gate that matters in this run is expo export completing over a real pnpm symlink to @huntstack/shared, and only a screen that actually fetches gets us there.

AMBIGUITY, TWO READINGS, ONE RECOMMENDATION. Reading A: v1 is the scaffold plus the flagship vertical slice, and the remaining screens are a second run, opened once apps/mobile/ is on main and a real fan-out becomes possible over files that exist. Reading B: v1 ports all three killer features now. I recommend A and have planned only A. Under A, run 2 is where the diamond finally earns its cost - with the scaffold on main, a Migration slice (app/(tabs)/migration/**), a Chat slice (app/(tabs)/chat/** plus AsyncStorage history) and a Regulations slice touch genuinely disjoint route directories and can fan out three ways. Choosing B now buys nothing that A does not buy later, and pays for it with a merge risk that only exists today.

DECISIONS MADE SO THE BUILDER DOES NOT HAVE TO. Scaffold: pnpm dlx create-expo-app@latest mobile --template default, run from huntstack/apps; SDK unpinned at latest but asserted at 53 or above and the resolved version recorded. Router: expo-router, not bare React Navigation. pnpm and Metro: START ISOLATED, no nodeLinker change; hoisting is the documented fallback only, and if used it drags a mandatory api-plus-web regression proof with it. API client: mobile writes its own roughly 150-line client for five endpoints; apps/web/src/lib/api.ts is NOT copied, because line 1 is import.meta.env and the file is 700 lines of inline types for endpoints we do not need. @huntstack/shared IS taken as a workspace:* dep - same app, therefore legal, and it doubles as the symlink canary. Base URL: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL, dev-defaulting to the LAN host derived from the expo-constants hostUri, because localhost:4000 is unreachable from a phone or an emulator and apps/api already binds 0.0.0.0; no hardcoded production URL, since CURRENT_STATE.md:299 records that the prod domain lives only in Cloudflare and Railway env vars. CORS: this run does NOT touch apps/api. A native React Native fetch is not a browser - it neither triggers a preflight nor enforces the response header, and @fastify/cors does not reject a request that carries no Origin. Spending a slice on apps/api/src/index.ts:50 would modify a production-serving file to fix a problem that does not exist; the MODERATE CORS risk the scout raised is real only for the Expo web target, which v1 does not build. CI: wired in, four steps, not deferred. Docs: CURRENT_STATE.md and CONSTRAINTS.md both verified present on disk before planning edits to them, per CLAUDE.md:465.

HUMAN-READ INSTRUCTIONS - the orchestrator runs this with the user; I could not.
SETUP. Two terminals, both from huntstack/. (1) `pnpm --filter @huntstack/api dev` and read the port it prints. apps/api defaults PORT to 4000 and the app derives :4000, but huntstack/CLAUDE.md:291 documents dev:api as 4001 - if the API binds anything other than 4000, create apps/mobile/.env with `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://<laptop-LAN-IP>:<port>` before starting Metro, or the phone will fail with a well-formed URL pointing at a closed port and no hint why. (2) `pnpm --filter @huntstack/mobile start`, then open the QR in Expo Go. The phone MUST be on the same wifi as the laptop; localhost is not routable from a phone, which is the whole reason the base URL is derived from the Metro host.
DO THIS FIRST, BEFORE JUDGING ANYTHING. Open the Settings tab and read the API row. It shows the resolved base URL and, underneath, whether it came from EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL or was derived from the Metro host. Then paste that same URL + `/api/hunt/recommendations` into a laptop browser. That single step separates 'the screen is broken' from 'the API returned nothing', and everything below depends on knowing which.
THE FOUR THINGS TO CONFIRM.
1. REAL API ROWS, NOT FIXTURES. The refuge names on the cards must match the `locationName` values in the browser JSON, in the same order, and each card's number badge must match `rank`. There are no fixtures anywhere in the app - the only invented refuge names in the repo are inside src/lib/*.test.ts, which vitest runs and Metro never bundles. The tell for a fixture would be seeing 'Muleshoe National Wildlife Refuge' when the browser shows something else.
2. GRANTING LOCATION RELABELS THE HEADER. Tap the round ◎ button to the right of the text field and Allow. Expect FOUR changes: the nav header title changes from 'Where to Hunt' to a reverse-geocoded place such as 'Amarillo, TX'; a line 'Distances from Amarillo, TX' appears under the field; a 'Best first / Closest first' pair appears; and every card whose refuge has a centre point gains ' · NN mi'. Tapping 'Closest first' must reorder without any spinner - it re-sorts in memory and does not re-fetch. Note the tab LABEL stays 'Where to Hunt'; only the header title changes. If the header shows coordinates like '35.222, -101.831' instead of a place name, GPS worked and the reverse geocode did not - that is the deliberate fallback, not a crash, and it is worth reporting separately.
3. DENYING LEAVES MANUAL ENTRY WORKING. Best done on a second device or after clearing the app's permission in OS settings. Deny the prompt: an amber line reads 'Location is off for HuntStack. Type a ZIP code or a town below instead.' The field must still be enabled. Type 79101 and hit the keyboard's search key - the header relabels to 'Amarillo, TX' and distances appear exactly as in (2). Then try a non-ZIP: 'Stuttgart, AR'. Both must work; a 5-digit string routes to /api/geo/zip and anything else to /api/geo/search. A bad ZIP must show the API's own message ('Invalid zip code'), not 'HTTP 400'.
4. TAPPING A ROW OPENS A POPULATED scoreBreakdown. Tap anywhere on a card. The 'Why this spot' screen opens with a 'Why this score' card listing SEVEN factors - Count trend, Birds present, Season open, Weather, Push factors, Migration stage, Unusual spike - biggest contributor first, each with a bar and its point value. Compare the numbers against `scoreBreakdown` for that row in the browser JSON. Bars are scaled to that row's largest factor, not to a per-factor maximum, because apps/api does not publish maxima. Below it, Birds / Season / Weather cards.
WHAT AN EMPTY LIST MEANS - so it is not mistaken for a broken screen. If the API returns `"recommendations": []` the screen shows a heading 'Nothing ranked for <species>' and body text beginning 'This is not an error.' That IS the expected rendering and it is a pass of the empty state. I read apps/api/src/routes/hunt.ts to get this right rather than guessing: the count query (hunt.ts:132-170) applies NO date window - it takes the latest survey per location+species regardless of age - and nothing downstream drops rows, so the list is NOT gated on the season being open. An empty list therefore means there are no refuge_counts rows for that species in the V1 states, i.e. an empty or unreachable database, and a closed season still ranks normally with seasonScore 0 and a 'Season closed' tag. If the browser check in the setup step shows `[]`, items 1 and 4 above CANNOT be confirmed and the human-read should be recorded as partial rather than passed - items 2 and 3 still can be, because the location flow does not need rows.

Season labels are the only Intl path left (formatDateRange inside @huntstack/shared); I deliberately hand-rolled the thousands separator in formatCount so bird counts are NOT exposed to it. If a card shows 'Season open' with a mangled or missing date range while the API clearly sent seasonStart/seasonEnd, that is Hermes ICU and scout unknown 2 is still open. WHY THE SCREEN IS SHAPED THIS WAY.
NATIVE, NOT A WEB PORT: FlatList with keyExtractor and RefreshControl pull-to-refresh; the whole card is the tap target rather than a small 'details' link; species is a horizontally scrolling chip row rather than a select, so the current choice stays visible while the list reloads; a real loading state, a real empty state and a real error state with a Try again button, all three routed through one describeListState so they cannot drift apart.
LOCATION CHANGES DO NOT RE-FETCH. getHuntRecommendations is called with a null origin and the screen re-decorates rows with decorateRecommendation in a useMemo. That is why 'Closest first' is instant and why moving the location pin re-sorts a list already on screen instead of spending a round trip. The endpoint takes no coordinates, so nothing is lost by doing it client-side.
A STALE-RESPONSE GUARD, because it would have been a real bug: a requestId ref means a slow request for a previously selected species cannot overwrite a newer one.
DISTANCE SORT PUTS UNMEASURABLE ROWS LAST rather than dropping them or treating null as 0. A refuge with no centre point is still a real recommendation and silently hiding it would be worse than showing it without a distance. Tested.
MOBILE-FIRST CONVENTION, applied as the s2 review established it: the registry's `ui: responsive-web` describes huntstack's WEB UI, so the width tiers do not transfer to a native app, but the touch-target and reach rules do. Every Pressable is >= 44pt (TOUCH_TARGET in theme.ts, used by the chips, the GPS button, the clear button, the sort buttons and the retry button), adjacent targets are >= 8pt apart (SPACING.sm), and every body/label/input string is >= 16pt. The one exception is the tab bar label at 12pt, which is the react-navigation tab-bar convention and sits under a 44pt-tall tab.
PERSISTENCE: last species and last location via AsyncStorage. Nothing is fetched until both have been read back, so a cold start does not fire one request for the default and a second for the preference a moment later. A restored location is always re-tagged source 'manual' - a remembered fix is not fresh GPS, whatever it was last time.
DETAIL HANDOFF: lib/loadedResults.ts, a module-scoped array the list writes and the detail reads by key. The alternative was serialising a 30-field object with a nested breakdown into a route param, which would put the whole row in the deep link. The cost is honest and stated on screen: a cold deep link into /recommendation/<id> has no list in memory and says 'This recommendation is not loaded ... open it again from the Where to Hunt list' rather than rendering blanks. v1 does no offline caching by design (architect's not-doing item 5).
ROW IDENTITY is `${locationId}:${species}`, not locationId. With no species filter the API returns one row per location+species pair, so locationId alone is not unique and would collide as a FlatList key. Tested.
